titre: The deepest canyon in the world is not the Grand Canyon
accroche: In Tibet, a river has carved a gorge three times deeper than the Grand Canyon, and almost no one had run it before 2002.
contenu_vulgarise:
The Grand Canyon in Arizona, carved by the Colorado River, is probably the most photographed canyon in the world: about 1,800 meters deep at its lowest point. Yet it falls far short of a much lesser-known canyon: that of the Yarlung Tsangpo, in Tibet, where the river plunges in places to more than 5,300 meters, according to NASA surveys, nearly three times deeper. More recent measurements even claim up to 6,000 meters at its lowest point.

## The mechanism

The Yarlung Tsangpo rises near Mount Kailash, in western Tibet, then crosses the Tibetan Plateau for nearly 3,000 km before, at its eastern end, making a sharp turn to the south. It is there, between the peaks of Namcha Barwa (7,782 m) and Gyala Peri, that the river has carved its most spectacular gorge, over more than 500 km.

What makes this gorge exceptional is not the river's power alone, but where it sits: at the Namcha Barwa and Gyala Peri massif, geologists have identified what they call a “tectonic aneurysm,” an isolated zone where erosion, concentrated in a narrow, deep valley, thins the Earth's crust, which lets the hot, ductile rock beneath rise faster; that uplift in turn feeds erosion, in a self-sustaining loop. Dating of the rock exhumed in this massif gives an incision rate of about 3 millimeters per year over the last ten million years. It is in this same massif that the canyon reaches its deepest point.

## The shift

For a long time this canyon was just a blank spot on the maps. Its walls are so steep, and its climate so unstable, that several attempts to kayak down its upper gorges ended in fatal accidents. It was not until 2002 that a team of seven kayakers, led by the American filmmaker Scott Lindgren and supported by 93 people on the ground, completed the first full descent: after 45 days on the water, with no reliable maps, studying satellite images kilometer by kilometer.

At the canyon's exit, at the Indian border, the river is already down to just 660 meters in elevation: it then changes its name and becomes the Brahmaputra. The canyon is therefore not only a depth record: it is the still-active trace of a mountain that rises faster than water can level it.

repere.texte: In places, the Yarlung Tsangpo canyon exceeds 5,300 meters in depth (about three times the Grand Canyon of the Colorado) over more than 500 km in length.

carte.punch: The deepest canyon in the world is not in Arizona, but in Tibet.
carte.idee: Where the Yarlung Tsangpo bends around Mount Namcha Barwa, in Tibet, the river has carved a gorge that exceeds 5,300 meters in depth in places: three times the Grand Canyon. Part of its gorges was not run by kayak until 2002, after 45 days and several fatal attempts.

pour_aller_plus_loin.note: Details the discrepancies between the various depth estimates and the full geography of the canyon.

quiz.question: Why is the Yarlung Tsangpo canyon so much deeper than the Grand Canyon of the Colorado?
choix: Because the river is much wider there and carries far more sediment torn from the plateau
Because it cuts through softer volcanic rock, which the current digs out far more easily
Because it was carved by a glacier much wider and thicker than the Colorado's
Because it crosses a zone where erosion thins the crust and speeds the rise of deep rock
quiz.explication: At the Namcha Barwa and Gyala Peri massif, geologists have identified a “tectonic aneurysm”: extreme erosion thins the crust, which lets the hot rock beneath rise faster, an uplift that in turn feeds erosion. The Grand Canyon was carved into a plateau without this mechanism. The Yarlung Tsangpo is no wider there, the rock is not volcanic, and no glacier carved this gorge.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What maximum depth does the Yarlung Tsangpo canyon reach, according to the most recent measurements?
choix: About 1,800 meters, the same depth as the Grand Canyon of the Colorado
Up to 6,000 meters at its lowest point, according to more recent measurements
About 3,000 meters, twice the Grand Canyon
More than 8,000 meters, the elevation of Mount Namcha Barwa
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The card states that more recent measurements claim up to 6,000 meters at the canyon's lowest point, far ahead of the roughly 1,800 meters of the Grand Canyon.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who led the first complete kayak descent of the upper gorges of the Yarlung Tsangpo, in 2002?
choix: A team of seven kayakers led by the American filmmaker Scott Lindgren, supported by 93 people on the ground
A lone Tibetan mountaineer, with no logistical support, following NASA maps
A NASA scientific expedition equipped with drones to map the canyon
A Chinese army team, which mapped the canyon before opening a tourist road
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The card specifies that the first complete descent of the upper gorges was made in 2002 by seven kayakers led by Scott Lindgren, supported by 93 people on the ground, after 45 days on the water.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the Yarlung Tsangpo become after crossing the Indian border, at 660 meters in elevation?
choix: It flows directly into the Indian Ocean under its Tibetan name
It joins the Ganges before forming a single delta
It disappears into an underground lake before resurfacing in Bangladesh
It changes its name and becomes the Brahmaputra
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text specifies that at the canyon's exit, at the Indian border, the river is already down to just 660 meters in elevation: it then changes its name and becomes the Brahmaputra.
